original_question: Let V be an external field on C, meaning a continuous function V : C -> R union {+infinity}, not identically +infinity, such that lim_{|z| -> infinity} (V(z) - log(1 + |z|)) = +infinity. For each n, let P_n be the unique monic polynomial of degree n satisfying the orthogonality relations integral_C P_n(z) z^k e^{-n V(z)} dA(z) = 0 for k = 0, 1, ..., n - 1, and let nu(P_n) be its normalized zero counting measure. Find external fields V for which nu(P_n) converges weakly to a limit measure mu_V as n -> infinity, and characterize the limiting measure mu_V.
target_in_paper: The draft targets the unnumbered open problem in Arno Kuijlaars’s section "Orthogonal polynomials in the complex plane with varying exponential weights and their limiting zero counting measures," stated immediately after the definitions of the external field, the zero counting measure, and the orthogonality conditions (1) and (2). ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation: it uses the same notion of external field on C, the same growth condition at infinity, the same degree-n monic polynomial defined by planar orthogonality against z^k e^{-nV(z)} dA for k=0,1,...,n-1, and the same goal of determining when the normalized zero counting measures converge weakly and characterizing the limit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
missing_details: The paper explicitly defines the normalized zero counting measure by first listing the zeros z_1,...,z_n of a monic degree-n polynomial with multiplicities and then setting ν(P)=n^{-1}∑_{j=1}^n δ_{z_j}; your draft names ν(P_n) but does not spell this out. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
The notation dA is identified in the paper as the area measure on the complex plane; your draft uses dA without defining it. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The paper’s convergence question is about weak convergence of probability measures on C; your draft says "converges weakly" but does not explicitly say the ambient space of measures is the space of probability measures on C. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The paper adds that the radial case V(z)=V(|z|) is trivial: then P_n(z)=z^n for every n and ν(P_n)=δ_0. A fully paper-faithful stand-alone version should acknowledge that the interesting content is really beyond this trivial class. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))

The nearby context warns that, unlike the real-line analogue, the complex-plane limit should not simply be assumed to equal the planar equilibrium measure in the external field; known examples instead produce a limit supported on a contour inside the convex hull of the support of the equilibrium measure. Your draft does not mention this crucial qualitative caution. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
refined_question: Let P be a monic polynomial of degree n with zeros z_1,...,z_n counted with multiplicity, and define its normalized zero counting measure by ν(P)=n^{-1}∑_{j=1}^n δ_{z_j}. Let V: C → R ∪ {+∞} be a continuous external field, not identically +∞, such that lim_{|z|→∞}(V(z)-log(1+|z|))=+∞. For each n∈N, let P_n be the unique monic polynomial of degree n satisfying the planar orthogonality conditions ∫_C P_n(z) z^k e^{-nV(z)} dA(z)=0 for k=0,1,...,n-1, where dA denotes area measure on C. Determine which external fields V—especially beyond the trivial radial case V(z)=V(|z|), for which P_n(z)=z^n and ν(P_n)=δ_0—have the property that the sequence {ν(P_n)} converges weakly, as n→∞, to a probability measure μ_V on C, and characterize the limiting measure μ_V. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
justification: This refinement stays with the exact open problem actually stated in the paper rather than broadening it. The draft is not aiming at a conjecture or theorem elsewhere in the article; rather, it is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Kuijlaars’s unnumbered "Problem" in the section on complex orthogonal polynomials with varying exponential weights. I only made explicit the paper’s own hidden notation and nearby qualifiers: the definition of ν(P), the meaning of dA, the fact that the radial case is trivial, and the contextual warning that the complex-plane limit should not be conflated with the planar equilibrium measure. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2312.07754v1))
